article_content: River Plate is taking measures to mitigate the effects of high altitude on their players during an upcoming match against San Jose in the Copa Libertadores. The team will be given a combination of Viagra, coffee, and aspirin to help improve oxygen circulation and breathing. Additionally, players have rented oxygen masks to wear during the game. The team's doctor explained that the medication is intended to counteract the effects of altitude sickness, which can cause breathing difficulties. The Estadio Jesus Bermudez, where San Jose plays their home games, is situated nearly 3,800 meters above sea level.

article_content: The Tourism and Transport Forum has released a report outlining proposed reforms to attract more Kiwi tourists to Australia. The reforms include cutting the Passenger Movement Charge from $55 to $25 and introducing a common visa for Asian tourists. The goal is to make it easier and cheaper for New Zealanders to visit Australia, with the potential to increase visitor numbers by up to 200,000 by 2020. According to Tourism Australia data, there were 1.21 million New Zealand visitor arrivals in 2013, although holiday visitors actually declined last year. The report aims to address this decline by streamlining check-in and customs procedures, making flying from New Zealand to Australia like a domestic service, and reducing travel times by around 25 per cent.

Ehdotukset sisältävät rahaa liikenneväylän maksun alentamista 55 dollariin 25 dollariin ja yhteisen viisumin esittelyjen käyttöönottoa Aasian matkailijoille. Tavoitteena on tehdä helpottaa uusiammatkailijoita Uuteen Australiaan, mikä voisi lisätä vierailijamäärää jopa 200 000:aan vuoteen 2020. Australian matkailuviraston mukaan oli 1,21 miljoonaa Uuden-Seelantiin vierailevaa vuonna 2013, vaikkaa lomakkeetilaiset vähenneet todellakin vähenee viime. Raportti pyrkii osoittaa tätä kosketteiden ja tullauksen menettelyjen, mikä tekisi lennosta Uudesta-Seelannista Australiaan lentoon matkustaa kuin domestic-palvelun kaltaiseen, ja vähentäisä matkustaa noin 25 prosenttia. article_content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has requested that China provide additional data on a mysterious respiratory illness that is spreading in the north of the country.
